title: Two Shipments, One Driver
description: One driver can legitimately be booked for two different shipments on two different days — that's not a bug, that's a normal week. Prove the two assignments stay cleanly separate rows rather than colliding on the driver.
successCondition: Assign the same driverId to two different shipments (shipment A and shipment B) with non-overlapping time windows (e.g. different days). Both PUT calls succeed with 200. Querying the assignments table via `npm run db:psql` (select shipment_id, driver_id from assignments where driver_id = '<driver id>') confirms exactly 2 rows, one per shipment_id, both correctly referencing the same driver_id — Assignment.shipmentId's @unique constraint scopes uniqueness per shipment, not per driver, so this is expected and correct.
hints: Assignment.shipmentId carries the @unique constraint in prisma/schema.prisma, not driverId — nothing stops the same driver from appearing in multiple assignment rows.
GET /api/fleet/conflicts should report nothing for this pair, since the time windows don't overlap — a good sanity check that this isn't secretly a conflict scenario.
